partners.mechanism_chain: EDAR (HGNC:2992) —DISRUPTS→ Abnormal ectodermal development (HP:0001074); EDAR (HGNC:2992) —LEADS_TO→ Hypohidrosis (HP:0000989); EDAR (HGNC:2992) —LEADS_TO→ Hair and nail abnormalities (HP:0001075); FAS (HGNC:3488) —DISRUPTS→ Lymphocyte apoptosis (GO:0006919); Lymphocyte apoptosis (GO:0006919) —DECREASES→ Lymphoproliferation (HP:0002746); Lymphocyte apoptosis (GO:0006919) —DECREASES→ Autoimmune cytopenias (HP:0001887); FAS (HGNC:3488) —LEADS_TO→ Lymphoproliferation (HP:0002746); FAS (HGNC:3488) —LEADS_TO→ Autoimmune cytopenias (HP:0001887). Mutations in EDAR lead to ectodermal dysplasia (Phenotype B), while mutations in FAS lead to impaired lymphocyte apoptosis and ALPS (Phenotype A). Although EDAR and FAS are distinct genes, both are involved in cellular signaling pathways that are critical for proper immune cell development and homeostasis, albeit through different mechanisms. partners.mechanism_chain: TNFRSF13B (HGNC:11776) —DISRUPTS→ B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050727); B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050727) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal hair and nail development (HP:0001002); B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050727) —LEADS_TO→ Recurrent bacterial infections (HP:00114210); B cell receptor signaling pathway (GO:0050727) —LEADS_TO→ Hypogammaglobulinemia (HP:0004324). Mutations in TNFRSF13B (encoding TACI) disrupt the B cell receptor signaling pathway. In ectodermal dysplasia 10A, this disruption leads to abnormal hair and nail development (HP:0001002). In common variable immunodeficiency 2, the same disruption results in hypogammaglobulinemia (HP:0004324) and recurrent bacterial infections (HP:00114210) due to impaired B cell maturation and antibody production.

partners.mechanism_chain: EDAR (HGNC:18487) —DISRUPTS→ Ectodermal appendage development (GO:0001713); Ectodermal appendage development (GO:0001713) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal dysplasia (HP:0001048); TNFRSF11B (HGNC:11979) —INCREASES→ RANKL signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1909846); RANKL signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1909846) —LEADS_TO→ Juvenile Paget disease (MONDO:0009394); RANKL signaling pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1909846) —LEADS_TO→ Ectodermal appendage development (GO:0001713). #### 1. ectodermal dysplasia 10B, hypohidrotic/hair/tooth type, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.686)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5669034)

Mutations in the EDAR gene disrupt its function, leading to impaired ectodermal-mesenchymal signaling. This disruption affects the development of hair, nails, teeth, and sweat glands, manifesting as various forms of ectodermal dysplasia.

**How to falsify it:** If pathogenic variants in EDAR are not identified in individuals with either disease, or if the identified variants do not map to functionally significant regions of the EDAR protein, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: The presence of common, benign variants in EDAR within the gnomAD database at a frequency significantly higher than expected for rare disease alleles would also challenge this hypothesis.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of EDAR in these related ectodermal dysplasias could lead to a unified therapeutic strategy targeting the ectodermal-mesenchymal signaling pathway, potentially benefiting patients with either condition.
